answer: A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a fleet in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, because each account consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. The knoll cap is enforced at intake and forge exposes the per-origin counts. At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a kernel tag. That is 7 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
